## How it works

- [statement] PBO needs the full set of trials. Hiding trials makes the test understate overfitting (the authors compare it to removing non-responders from a drug trial), and for guided searches the matrix columns should hold each search's final converged result, not its intermediate steps. Bailey and López de Prado add that PBO is non-parametric but 'requires a large amount of information'. The PBO paper also lists design limits: strong autocorrelation in the performance series can make the symmetric block division obscure it, especially when S is large. (medium confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf
- [statement] Keep a trial ledger from the first experiment: every signal variant, feature, horizon, asset and threshold tried, with its full P&L series, failures included. The ledger supplies N, the variance of trial Sharpe ratios for DSR, and the T-by-N matrix that PBO needs. Bailey and López de Prado say investors and referees should demand the trial count, and that multiple-testing exercises should be planned in advance because each extra trial raises the false-positive probability. Whether correlated variants count as one trial or many is a judgement to disclose. (medium confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Constrain the search with theory before computing anything. Bailey and López de Prado say investment theory, not computational power, should decide which experiments are worth running, and suggest an optimal-stopping rule: sample roughly 37% of the theoretically justified configurations, then take the first that beats all of them. Harvey, Liu and Zhu say a factor derived from first principles can face a lower hurdle than one found by empirical search. For order-flow or funding signals, a mechanism written down before the test shrinks N and defends a lower bar; that application is an inference from the two papers. (medium confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P118_and_the_cross.PDF

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A backtest's Sharpe ratio cannot be interpreted without the number of independent trials behind it. Even if every strategy has zero true skill, the best Sharpe among N independent trials rises with N, so more searching produces better-looking winners; Bailey and López de Prado give an extreme-value approximation for this expected maximum. They call the number of trials attempted the most important piece of information missing from virtually all published backtests, and say a backtest whose author has not controlled for the extent of the search is 'worthless, regardless of how excellent the reported performance might be'. Harvey, Liu and Zhu make the same point from the other side: failed tests are never published, so the number of factors tested is unobservable. (high confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P118_and_the_cross.PDF, https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf
- [statement] The Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) is a Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio whose rejection threshold is raised to reflect the multiplicity of trials. Beyond the mean and standard deviation of returns it needs five more inputs: skewness, kurtosis, sample length T, the variance of Sharpe ratios across trials, and the number of independent trials N. Non-normality matters because negative skew and fat tails can inflate a Sharpe ratio; Harvey and Liu raise the same caveat for option-like strategies with negative skew. (medium confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P120_Backtesting.pdf
- [statement] Fill and latency assumptions can erase a fast signal's edge, and a replay backtest cannot test them. HftBacktest's documentation says a market-data replay cannot change the market, so one of the most important assumptions is that your order is small enough to have no impact; some partial-fill cases and large liquidity-taking fills may be unrealistic; and you must test in a live market and adjust the backtest to the discrepancies. For passive orders it offers a conservative RiskAverseQueueModel (queue position advances only when a trade prints at your price) and a probabilistic ProbQueueModel. It supports only market-by-price depth, which most crypto venues provide, so queue position must be estimated. It also separates feed latency (handled with local and exchange timestamps), order-entry latency and order-response latency. (medium confidence) — https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/order_fill.html · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/latency_models.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The cleanest out-of-sample evidence is a forward test of the exact strategy on new data. Harvey and Liu say a true out-of-sample test of the particular strategy, as opposed to a hold-out of historical data, is cleaner but unavailable for most strategies. HftBacktest's documentation says a replay-based result must be checked in a live market with real participants and the backtest adjusted to the gap. For a fast signal this points to a small, logged shadow or live run whose fills, fees and latency are compared with the backtest's assumptions before sizing up. (medium confidence) — https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P120_Backtesting.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/order_fill.html
- [statement] Overfitting can be worse than zero skill. Bailey and López de Prado argue that for financial series with memory, the extreme in-sample patterns that backtest overfitting selects are later undone, so overfitting leads to 'loss maximization' out of sample rather than merely no gain. Harvey and Liu, summarising López de Prado and coauthors, say only seven trials are needed to obtain a spurious two-year backtest with an in-sample Sharpe ratio above 1.0 while the expected out-of-sample Sharpe ratio is zero. (medium confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P120_Backtesting.pdf

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Multiple-testing statistics fix selection bias only; they do not check that the backtest is correct. The PBO paper says its procedure 'does nothing to evaluate the correctness of a backtest', and names incorrect transaction costs and use of data not available at decision time as errors that would feed it flawed information. Harvey and Liu state that the Sharpe ratios in their worked examples reflect no transaction costs, so they are overstated 'before-costs' figures. Remove cost, fill, latency and timestamp errors first, then count trials and deflate the net, decision-time-correct returns. (high confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing · also: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P120_Backtesting.pdf
- [statement] Do not trust equal-weighted or small, illiquid universe backtests. Novy-Marx and Velikov find anomaly spreads are often larger in smaller stocks, but those stocks are much costlier to trade, so equal-weighted results are 'misleading and should be viewed skeptically' and often show worse net performance. By analogy (an inference, not tested in the paper), a signal that looks strongest on thin altcoin perpetuals deserves the most cost and impact scrutiny. (low confidence) — https://mysimon.rochester.edu/novy-marx/research/ToAatTC.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing
- [statement] A passing PBO does not certify the regime, and a high PBO does not prove absence of skill. The PBO paper says the procedure accounts for structural breaks only if they occur inside the dataset; if a break lies outside it, the strategy may be overfit to one regime and PBO will not show it, so the data must be representative of future states. If all tested strategies have high and similar Sharpe ratios, none stands out and PBO is high even though skill exists. (low confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf · keywords: Honest signal evaluation out of sample costs and multiple testing
